records.c: The map of sections 0 and 1, read backwards two bytes a block row from $07FA (section 0) or $05FE (section 1, the boat), each byte a 16-by-4-character block at $9B12 for the left and right halves of the road. The road with its bridges and side roads comes first, then the water with its piers, ending at the dock at $0400.
Five bytes after the map's first row, not read as map.
The zero byte that comes before a BASIC program, at the start of BASIC memory.
Fifteen zero bytes where a BASIC line would sit. The code after them starts at $0810 (2064).

Not part of the game: a resident stub for a development computer connected by a parallel cable to the user port (data on $DD01, handshake on $DD00 bits 2 and 3). Entered at $0810, it saves the caller's registers at $09D2-$09D9 and then obeys one-byte commands from the cable: $B4 receive a block into memory, $B6 send a block back, $B5 and $BA set the address the stub calls at $098A and run it, $B7 set the memory banking used for transfers ($01), $B8 and $B9 send or receive the saved registers. It is how the game's code reached the C64 while it was written; on this disk it was called last to run the routine at $0A00.
The low byte of a receive's length ($B4), kept as the operand of the LDA at $088A and counted down.
The high byte of a receive's length, the operand of the LDA at $088E.
The page a receive writes to, the high byte of the STA at $08A0; set from the command and moved on every 256 bytes. Left at $CB on this disk.
The low byte of a send's length ($B6), the operand of the LDA at $08E1.
The high byte of a send's length, the operand of the LDA at $08E5.
The page a send reads from, the high byte of the LDA at $08F4; moved on every 256 bytes.
The instruction the stub runs for commands $B5 and $BA: $B5 stores a JSR opcode here and an address in the next two bytes, $BA stores all three bytes from the cable. Left as JSR $0A00.
The low byte of the address called at $098A.
The high byte of the address called at $098A.
Waits for the development computer's strobe on $DD00 bit 2, reads a byte from $DD01 and acknowledges by flipping bits 2 and 3 of $DD00.
The handshake state, kept as the operand of the EOR at $0993: the $DD00 bits (2 and 3) the stub sets next and expects back. Starts at $08.
Puts A on $DD01, signals on $DD00 and waits for the other side's answer.
The development stub's saved registers, seven bytes moved as one by commands $B8 and $B9: the caller's status flags here, then A, X, Y, the stack pointer and the return address (high byte first).
The caller's A, saved by the stub at $082F.
The caller's X.
The caller's Y.
The caller's stack pointer, put back before the call at $098A.
The high byte of the caller's return address, read from the stack.
The low byte of the caller's return address.
The memory banking ($01) used while bytes are moved and while the call at $098A runs; set by command $B7. Not among the seven bytes $B8 and $B9 move.

The game's own BASIC line (SYS 2064) runs the start-up at $0810, which calls here. When the disk was mastered these three bytes were set to JMP $0A00, a loop on itself: the start-up ran into it, the machine was frozen with Trilogic's Expert cartridge, and the restart routine resumes at $0A03. Nothing jumps here again.

The game's first instruction after the hand-over. Moves the charset and the overlay out of the VIC bank into the RAM under the I/O area ($2885), blanks the screen, clears the panel screen's page at $8300, installs the raster interrupts ($115B), clears zero page from $22 up, silences the music player (tune 0 at $F087), swaps the overlay in to run its set-ups at $44FA, $4599 and $4605, picks VIC bank 1 ($DD00 = 2) with screen $7800 and charset $7000 ($D018 = $EC), clears the score and the Q-token count, gives 5 lives ($44), and starts section 0, the harbour road ($198A with X = 0). Falls into the main loop at $0A94.

One pass of play. When a scroll stop has been reached ($79) and the car is standing still and alive, runs the section's end ($26E4). Counts $78 down and, when it reaches 0, clears the screen ($1944) and starts section 4. Steps the water animation ($27EE), the sprite-slot bookkeeping at $A5, every object's update ($8400), the speed from the car's height ($341F), the keyboard ($3724) and the sprite sort ($1BD0). While $9C is 0 it runs the spawner ($0C17) and builds the next map row in advance ($0D0D); otherwise it waits a frame. Adds the speed $82 to the fine scroll $83: when it passes 8 the new row is drawn ($0FC3), otherwise only the fine scroll moves. Then the timers ($38FA), and unless the controls are locked ($42): collisions with the player ($2A39), and the tile under the car (kind from table $E872): kinds 5, 6 and 9 kill the car, 4 jolts it and makes smoke ($391D) when it is moving up the screen, 10 kills it in a water section unless $45 is still running, 8 and 13 put it back where it was and reverse its sideways speed, 3 calls $39B4 on land. Then enemy shots ($2B9F), the player's shots ($2ABF, $368D, $34C0, $363F) and the panel ($2981). While the car has armour left ($96F0) it loops; at 0 it loses a life ($44), throws the wreck ($3357) and sets the dying animation, which ends in $3979.

Hides the sprites and swaps the overlay in ($28B6), calls its routine at $428C, swaps it out, turns the interrupt's sprite work back on ($3F = 0) and asks for the sprite registers to be rewritten ($97 = 1).
Swaps the overlay in, runs its routine at $4187, and swaps it out again (JMP to the swap, so the swap's RTS returns to the caller).
Runs $0C08, then jumps back into the start-up at $0A53 to restart the game from the title state.

Called every pass while the map scrolls. ($10) walks the section's spawn list, three bytes an entry: two distance bytes, each compared with the scroll counter $A3/$A4 (which counts down), then a kind byte. Bits 0-4 of the kind byte pick one of the 32 spawn routines at $8EB3; bits 5-7 are a parameter left in $8A for the routine. The parameter also gives the start y ($8EA7) and, from its low two bits, where it enters across: the left road edge ($17F9), the right road edge ($180D), or 16 pixels inside either (in open water the fixed x at $8EAF). Fills the object template at $22-$3B with defaults ($0CD6), advances ($10) past the entry and jumps to the spawn routine, which usually ends at $0C9B or $2782.

Copies the 26-byte object template at $22-$3B into the first of the 31 slots after the player whose y (byte 2) is 0. Gives up quietly when none is free. When $33 is set, also stores the new slot's address into bytes $11-$12 of the object last added by $2782 (left in $06), linking that part to this object.

Fills the object template at $22-$3B with the defaults every spawn starts from: animation delay 2, hit points 5, frame $10, flags clear, animation script $90CF, handler $30AC (the do-nothing handler), no hardware sprite ($37 = $FF).

Prepares the next map row ahead of time; the main loop calls it once after each new row is shown (it sets $9C, which $0FC3 clears). Counts down the two timers at $45 and $46. Unless the car is in the Q-truck sequence ($7C), and once $46 has run out, adds the speed's score ($8603 indexed by speed $82, 7 further on when $40 is set) to the BCD score at $9D-$A0. Shifts the two 32-entry road-edge histories at $B3 and $D3 down one, builds the new top row of characters and colours from the map: the map at ($02) holds two bytes a row, each a 4-row by 16-character block number at $9B12 (64 bytes a block, row $87 within it), or $3040 further on when the alternative tile set is in ($4D). Colours come from table $E782 by character, or the fixed colour $4E with the alternative set. Then finds the new road edges ($0F30), counts the distance down ($A3/$A4), steps to the next block row of the map, and shifts the whole character and colour buffers down a row.
Road edges for an open-water section ($68 of 2 or more): left 64, right 192.

Finds where the road (or the channel) is in the new top row of the character buffer, for the spawner and the enemies that follow the road. In a road section ($68 = 0) it looks for the tile kinds 2 or 13 (the right edge) from the right and 1 or 13 (the left edge) from the left, and stores their x as $D3 and $B3. In a water section ($68 = 1) it uses the pier kinds 11 and 12. In open water the edges are fixed ($0F27).

Copies the 20 visible rows of the character buffer ($E262) into the hidden screen ($7C04 or $7804, chosen by $9B), clears $9C so the next row can be prepared, waits for the frame ($1152), copies the new fine-scroll values into the copies the interrupt reads, flips $9B so the next frame shows the screen just drawn, points the sprite-pointer address ($0C) at that screen's $3F8, and then copies the colour buffer ($E502) into colour memory at $D804.
Copies 20 rows of 32 bytes from ($04) to ($06), stepping the destination by 40 (a screen row) and the source by 32. Unrolled.
Finds a free entry among the 15 shots of 15 bytes at $9A22 (free when byte 8 is 0) and fills it from the template at $22-$31: x, y and the rest. Used by enemies that fire.
Waits X times the inner delay at $1130 (each about 1,280 cycles).
A busy wait of 256 loops of DEX/BNE, keeping X in $8600.
Waits until the raster has just entered the bottom border: first until bit 7 of $D011 is clear, then until it is set (line 256 or later).
Sets $3C and waits for the raster interrupt at $1B3E/$11BB to clear it, so the caller runs once a frame.

Sets $01 to $35 (KERNAL and BASIC out), turns off the CIA interrupts, turns on the raster interrupt, points the NMI vector at an RTI ($119E) so RESTORE does nothing, the IRQ vector at $128C, the end-of-frame call ($8601) at $119F, and the first raster line at $C8.
An RTI: the NMI vector points here, so RESTORE does nothing.
The default end-of-frame routine reached through ($8601): steps the random number at $80 (times 5 plus 1, an 8-bit linear congruential sequence) and clears $3C, which releases $1152.
Points the end-of-frame call ($8601/$8602) at X:Y with interrupts held off.

Raster interrupt at line $D9, the top of the panel: turns the screen into extended background mode with the display on until line $DA, then normal ($D011 = $10), arms the next interrupt at line $F7 ($11F4) and runs the music player ($E9E1) once a frame.

Raster interrupt at line $F7, in the lower border, which sets up the next frame of the play area: vertical and horizontal fine scroll from $83 and $84, black background, VIC bank 1, screen $7800 or $7C00 (by $9B), multicolours $AD and $AE, the next interrupt at line $32. When the game is not between screens ($3F = 0) the next interrupt is the sprite multiplexer at $1B3E, and the sprite sizes and multicolour flags ($94-$96) are written when $97 asks; all eight sprites are parked at y 0 and the multiplexer is entered at once. Otherwise the next is the panel at $128C.

Raster interrupt that switches to the panel at line $CF: waits for the line, delays by the fine scroll ($8851 indexed by $83) so the switch lands on the right line, writes $D011 from $8859, VIC bank 2 ($DD00 = 1) with both the screen and the charset based at $8000 ($D018 = 1), multicolours 11 and 12, arms $11BB at line $D9 and leaves through the end-of-frame call ($8601).
An RTI followed by four NOPs, which nothing reaches.
Sets the processor port: data direction $2F and $01 = $35 (I/O in, BASIC and KERNAL out).
Object handler: keeps level with the car ($13D9), then steers towards the left road edge at its height ($17F9), changing its x speed by one a pass, up to 3 either way.

Object handler: keeps level with the car ($13A0); one pass in 32 ($80), while it is above the car, counts $8C down (when it reaches 0 the object turns to $13A3 with +7 set to $50 and y speed -8) and, one time in four, adds one of the road spawns $1E64, $1E7B, $1E92 or $1EA9 below it.
Object handler: aims at 32 pixels inside the right road edge ($180D) and steers there ($13A8).
Object handler: may fire up the screen ($16BC), keeps level with the car ($13D9) and follows the right road edge ($13A3).
Object handler: keeps level with the car ($13D9) and follows the right road edge ($13A3).
Object handler: steers towards 16 pixels inside the right road edge at its height ($180D), changing its x speed by one a pass, up to 3 either way. Its target x is left in $7D.

Matches the object's y speed to the car's: while the controls are locked ($42), or $69 or $45 is set, it moves up the screen at y speed -8. Otherwise it speeds up or slows down by one a pass (between -8 and -1) to stay at the offset +18 from the car.
Object handler: follows the right road edge ($13A3), leaves its x speed in $71 and sets $72 and its y speed to -8.

The Q-truck's handler. First time ($69 = 0) releases the objects with link ids $E2 and $01 ($27B7). Keeps level with the car ($13E8) and the right road edge ($13A3). While $69 is negative it pulls the car in: matches the car's speeds to its own, slides the car across to its x and up the screen, counting +18 up; when the car is 20 pixels inside, sets $69 to 1 and opens the shop ($0BF6). While $69 is positive the car backs out down the screen; at 67 pixels out the controls come back ($42, $69 cleared) and the handler becomes $1415.

Object handler: releases the object with link id $1E ($27B7); then, one pass in four, when its x is 0 to 9 pixels more than the car's, turns into a road follower ($13A3) with collision kind 10, and sets its linked child (+11/+12) moving: width 8, x speed 0, y speed -9, handler $30AC.
Object handler: follows the road ($13A0) and keeps its speeds in $73 and $74 for its children ($17BA).
Object handler: aims inside the right road edge ($1391) and keeps its speeds in $73 and $74.
Object handler: may fire ($16BC); once above y $46, picks one of eight animation scripts at random from $8F73 and becomes $154A.
Object handler: one pass in 16, when it is above the car and within 16 pixels across, drops a shot down the screen (y speed 3, life 24, 5 rows high).

Object handler: may aim at the car ($1617); one pass in 32 adds a child 48 pixels below and 24 to one side (frame $0C, collision kind $0D or $8D, script $946A or $9462 with handler $15FD), then keeps its speeds in $73 and $74.
Object handler: moves the object 1 pixel left, right or not at all at random.
Object handler: one pass in 16 at random fires a shot at the car ($36CD).

Handler of a large character-drawn enemy (with $16AD and $1821): holds still on the screen (y speed against the scroll, saved in $70) and keeps its position in $75/$76 for its parts. Near the top it drops 12 pixels, turns to $16AD and takes frame $A8. Drifts across towards the car by one a pass, up to 3 (saved in $6F); when the car is beside it fires two shots at the car 16 pixels apart ($36CD).
Like $162C, but stores y in $76 only until it passes $E6, then 0.
One pass in 16 (in four on water, $48), when the object is within 16 pixels across of the car and below it, fires a shot up the screen ahead of the scroll (life 24, 5 rows).
One pass in eight at random fires a shot at the car ($36CD).
One pass in 16 adds a laser object (frame $36, collision kind $87, 8 by 21, y speed 10) moving down from the object.

Handler of the homing weapon fired by $3B78: counts its life (+10) down; when it is within 16 pixels of the target ($75/$76) it hits the object at ($7A) through $2E76. When its life runs out it is removed (y 1, y speed -9).
Object handler: takes the boss's speeds ($6F, $70); frame $32 drops 12 pixels and becomes $A7 while it moves down.
Object handler: takes its speeds from $71 and $72.
Object handler: takes its speeds from $73 and $74, so it moves with its parent.
Object handler: places itself at $75 + 58 and $76 - 44, a part of the character-drawn enemy.
Object handler: outside the Q-truck sequence ($7C) removes itself; otherwise places itself at $75 + 80 and $76 - 44.
Returns in $7D the left road edge plus 16 at screen y A, from the history at $B3 (one entry per character row from y $32).
Returns in $7D the right road edge minus 16 at screen y A, from the history at $D3.

Handler of the large enemy drawn in characters. Keeps its x (up to $87) and y in $75/$76, blanks the top of the character buffer and draws its picture from $87C4 into the buffer, 16 characters a row, up to 8 rows (fewer near the top, offsets $86E1), so it scrolls with the map and its fine position follows it ($85/$86). One pass in 16 fires at the car from 68 pixels in ($36CD); one pass in 32 adds two lasers 74 pixels apart moving down (or up when it is below the car). Outside the Q-truck sequence ($7C) it removes itself.

Clears the play area with a dissolve: four times over, ANDs every byte of the charset ($7000-$77FF) with one of the masks at $8685, so the characters fade away in stages; then empties the buffers ($284E) and draws them ($0FC3). Every new section and every death starts with it.

Starts section X ($43): empties the sprite lists, draws the panel ($2981), frees every object ($2740), resets the car ($1ADF), swaps the overlay in, shows "well done" ($887C) unless $F3 is set, then "get ready" ($8861), swaps back and restores the road charset ($290B). Sets the start-up timer $46 to $15, multicolours 12 and 8, clears the flags of the last section ($68, $58, $48, $4A, $4C, $66, $7C, $79, $3F) and the alternative tile set, then sets the map ($02), distance ($A3/$A4) and spawn list ($10) for the section: 0 at $07FA/$88A4, 1 at $05FE/$8A03 (car at x $64), 2 at $969E/$8A7B (x $E0), 3 at $96BE/$8CD3 ($1A6A), 4 at $96D8/$8D6F ($1ABA).

Section 3: the map at $96BE, the second charset ($293D), open water ($68 = 2), spawn list $8CD3, fixed tile colour 15 ($4E), multicolours 9 and 5 and sprite multicolour 11, every sprite multicolour, $58 set, and the lasers, $5D and $5E given back from $62-$64.
Section 4: the map at $96D8, spawn list $8D6F, scene kind 3 ($68) and $48 = 3.
Clears $5A and $59, then resets the car ($1ADF).

Puts the car at x $80, y 1 with animation script $90CD, frees the controls, clears its speeds and every weapon ($5B-$61, $65), sets its size (14 by 19), frame $10, colour 15 and full armour ($96F0 = $FF).

The sprite multiplexer's raster interrupt. Reads the 7-byte entries of the list at ($08): sprite register offset, x, y, x high bit, colour, pointer and the raster line of the next entry. Writes each into the VIC (the pointer at ($0C), the screen being shown) and sets the next raster line; a line of 0 writes the next entry at once. At the end of the list or below line $B4 it arms the panel interrupt ($128C) at line $CC and points ($08) at the list just built ($B1/$B2).

Builds next frame's sprite list, alternating between $E000 and $E0E1 ($91). Sorts the objects by y into a table indexed by y ($0200 high bytes, $0300 low; a taken entry moves to the next). Objects that own a hardware sprite (+15) go straight into the list ($1C88). Then assigns the free sprites to the rest from the top ($1CFE) and reuses them lower down ($1D75). Ends the list, turns all sprites on and hands the list to the interrupt ($B1/$B2).
Adds the object at ($04) to the list on its own hardware sprite (+15): register offset, x + 40 and the high bit from $8611, y (kept in $CF7A), colour and frame.
Finds the next hardware sprite from $88 whose slot entry at $A5 is free, and returns its register offset in $8A and bit in $8B.
Gives the free hardware sprites to the objects in y order, from table index X up to $D7, until all eight are used ($8B goes negative). Then sets $93 to the lowest y that is free for reuse.

The multiplexer's second pass: gives each remaining object (index below $CA) the next hardware sprite, but only when it is at least 38 lines below that sprite's last use ($CF7A) and below the line $93. Each entry's raster line is the previous one plus 3, so writes happen before each sprite is drawn.
Spawn routine 0: a road vehicle, frame $45, colour 6, 20 by 18, collision kind $81, the default handler.
Spawn routine 1: a road vehicle, frame $44, colour 11, 20 by 18, collision kind $82.
Spawn routine 2: a road vehicle, frame $48, colour 8, 20 by 16, collision kind $83.
Spawn routine 3: a road vehicle, frame $46, colour 5, 20 by 18, collision kind $84.
Spawn routine 4: collision kind $85, 50 high, with animation script $8FB3 and colour 8 on land (8 wide), or script $8FD9 and colour 10 on water (16 wide).
Spawn routine 5: collision kind $86, colour 2: frame $1A, 10 by 14, on land; frame $49, 14 by 16, on water.

Spawn routine 7: a two-part enemy, collision kind 8, colour 15, 24 by 40, damage 10, score $25, handler $1617 (fires at the car). Parameter below 4: comes down from the top (y $EA, y speed -4, frame $BD) with a second part (frame $43) linked to it by $33 on handler $30AC. Otherwise moves down at speed 2 with frame $BF and a part with frame $BE.
Spawn routine 8: frame $1B, colour 8, 12 by 12, collision kind $89.
Spawn routine 9: an enemy car, frame 7, colour 11, 14 by 19, y speed -8, collision kind 10, damage 10, score $10, handler $13A3 (follows the right road edge).
Spawn routine 10: an enemy car, frame 5, colour 6, 14 by 19, y speed -7, collision kind 11, damage 10, score $10, handler $139D (keeps level and fires). Releases a waiting object ($27AD).

Spawn routine 11: frame 6, colour 2, 12 by 10, y speed -7, collision kind 12, damage 6, link id $28, handler $14B8. If an object with link id $28 is already there it changes its handler to $1518. Adds a part (frame $7A, kind $0D, handler $17BA) linked to it.

Spawn routine 13, only when hardware sprite 1 is free ($A6): a large object on fixed sprites, collision kind 14, from the top (y $EA) at y speed -7, 16 by 72, frame 8, damage 20, link id $D8, handler $1422 (the Q-truck), with two linked parts on sprite 1 and the next free sprite (frame 9, colour 11, handler $17AE), expanded across.

Spawn routine 14, only when sprite 1 is free: the boss on fixed sprites 1 and 2, collision kind 15, colour 11, from the top at y speed -7 (kept in $70), frame $31, score $25, handler $162C. Its body (frame $32, handler $178D) is linked to it and its address kept in $7A for the homing weapon; a third part (frame $2F, script $90D1, expanded, sprite 0) sits 11 pixels left.
Spawn routine 15: frame $0D, colour 2, 16 by 20, y speed -7, collision kind 16, damage 10, score $10, handler $139D. Releases a waiting object ($27AD).
Spawn routine 16: frame $98, colour 2, 14 by 20, y speed -7, collision kind 17, damage 10, score $10, handler $139D, animation script $9104. Releases a waiting object.
Spawn routine 19: collision kind $94, colour 7, 10 by 9, script $9015.
Spawn routine 20: frame $0A, colour 11, y speed 1, 14 by 19, collision kind $15, damage 10, score $10, handler $1300 (follows the left road edge).
Spawn routine 21: collision kind $16 and the defaults.

Spawn routine 22: frame $16, colour 2, 16 by 20, y speed -6, collision kind $17, damage 15, score $10, link id $E2, handler $1339 (drops other vehicles), with $8C set to 10. Releases the object with id $E2 ($27B7) first.
Spawn routine 23: frame $79, colour 11, 24 by 21, collision kind $98. With parameter 0 it is placed at x $30, 48 wide. On water ($48) it uses frame 2, 42 wide, on hardware sprite 6, expanded.

Spawn routine 17: collision kind $12, colour 2, 12 by 20. Coming from below the middle (y positive): one of eight random scripts at $8F73 and handler $154A (drops bombs). Otherwise script $9419, y speed -3 and handler $151E.

Spawn routine 18: a pickup at a random x from $40 to $BF (or at $10 or $E0 moving down for parameters 5 and 6), collision kind $13, 16 by 20, damage 1. The low bits of the parameter (below 5, else random) choose it: frame $69 upwards, 14 by 14, or with $58 set frame $37 upwards with colour from $86EA.
Spawn routine 24: a two-part enemy from the top (y $EA, y speed -4), collision kind $19, colour 12, 24 by 42, frame $41, damage 10, score $25, handler $1617, with a part (frame $42) linked on $30AC.

Spawn routine 25: collision kind $1A, which also sets $7C; script $911D. With parameter 0 one enemy ($2406) at x $80 and $77 = 1; otherwise two at $40 and $C0 (the second flipped) and $77 = 2, so $332D counts them.
Adds the enemy for $23D8: y 1, colour 7, 24 by 42, frame $34, damage 50, score $25, handler $1617, with a linked part (frame $33) on $30AC.

Spawn routine 26: collision kind $1B, handler $17BA, y speed -2, delay 8. Parameter 0 uses script $941E and handler $1586. Position from $86D3/$86DA by the parameter (parameter 6 also sets $7C), frame $B6 plus the parameter, colour 12, 20 by 20, damage 50, score $10, $77 = 4. Parameters above 0 are put straight into the slot before the first object of kind $1B ($24AA).
Spawn routine 27: collision kind $1C, colour 2, 14 by 19, from y $D2 at y speed -4, script $9472, handler $16BC (fires up).

Spawn routine 29: four objects, collision kind $1D, colour 11, damage 50, score $25: two 24 by 21 at x $60 and $A4 (script $9108, handler $1706), two at x $58 and $AC, y 8 (script $910E, handler $171B, which fire lasers down). Sprites lose their expand bits and $77 = 4.

Spawn routine 30: the large character-drawn ship. Multicolours 11 and 15, sets $7C, collision kind $1E, x $32, score $50, handler $1821, script $919A; a second object 48 by 80 (colour 7, frame $7B, handler $17C6, script $90CF), and a third (frame $7C, handler $17D9).
Spawn routine 28: sets $58, which swaps some frame numbers ($2712) and the shot pattern ($34C0, $3600). The spawn list uses it to change the look of later objects.

Spawn routine 31, the section's scripted event, with the event number in the spawn entry's parameter ($8A, bits 5-7 of its kind byte). 0 ($2643): sends away every object whose handler is $139D. 1: sets the distance counter to $03F2 and adds a large object on hardware sprite 0, expanded ($94/$95 bit 0), at x $58 with frame $8E and colour 12. 2 or more: $267F.
Event 0: every object whose handler is $139D gets handler $13A3 and a y speed of -12, so it leaves up the screen.

Events 3 to 6. 3: switches to the map at $969E with the spawn list at $8A7B, block row $20 and distance $07FF. 4: switches to the map at $96BE, makes every sprite multicolour and sets $4C, which changes the car's controls ($341F, $346E). 5: sets $7C. 6: sets $4C to $20 and switches to the map at $96D8. Any other number is stored in $7C and $79, which stops the scroll ($82 = 0) until the section ends ($0A94).
Clears the screen ($1944) and starts section 3 ($198A with X = 3).

The end of a section, run by the main loop at a scroll stop. Only while the car has armour ($96F0). Clears the screen ($1944); after section 1 starts section 2 at once. Otherwise empties both sprite lists ($E000, $E0E1), swaps the overlay in, shows the message at $8894 ($4364), swaps it out and starts again from section 0.

Adds a score sign where the object at ($04) is (its x and y), with the frame in X ($A4 -50, $A5 50, $A6 100; with $58 set, $A5 and $A6 become the other-coloured $5B and $5C), animation script $8F83 and the default handler ($0CD6). Called by the scoring at $2C9F and by $2FFA.
Entry into $2712 that keeps the x speed already in the template ($27), so several signs fan out ($2C9F).

Frees all 31 object slots after the player (y and the visible flag cleared), and resets the sprite-slot list ($96F7, $A6-$AC), the expand and multicolour bytes ($94-$96) and asks for the sprite registers to be rewritten ($97).
Copies the 26-byte object template at $22-$3B into the first of the 31 slots after the player whose y is 0. Gives up quietly when none is free. Unlike $0C9B it never links a child to a parent.
Picks a random link id from the eight at $86CB and releases the object carrying it: clears its id, gives it handler $1391 and a y speed of -12.
Releases the object whose link id (+18) matches $3A: clears the id, gives it handler $1391 (aim inside the right road edge) and a y speed of -12. Entry point inside $27AD for a chosen id.
Every other call (toggling $49), and only while $58 is clear, rotates four 8-byte character definitions in each of three groups ($7500-$751F, $7260-$727F, $7280-$729F), which makes the water ripple.
Fills the character buffer ($E242 onwards, three pages) with spaces ($20) and the colour buffer ($E4E2 onwards) with colour 1, and sets $85 to 7.
Copies 255 bytes from $CE53 to $76D9 and 40 from $CF52 to $77D8 (both loops stop before index 0).
Called once at start-up. With all RAM visible ($01 = $34), copies $7000-$7FFF (the charset and the overlay's code) to $D000-$DFFF, zeroing the source as it goes, then puts $01 back to $37.

Hides the sprites ($3F = $FF, all eight at y 0), then, one page per frame at the bottom border ($113C), swaps the eight pages $4000-$47FF with $D800-$DFFF under all-RAM banking ($01 = $30). Calling it twice puts both back.
Copies the charset kept under the I/O area ($D000-$D7FF) back to $7000, one page per frame, and clears $4D (normal tile set).
Copies the second charset at $F610-$FE0F to $7000 and sets $4D to 8 (the alternative tile set). Not seen running.
Writes the BCD byte in $16 as two digit characters (table $86F0) at ($14).

Draws the panel. Each time the score's hundred-thousands digit changes ($9E high nibble against $F6) gives a life. Lives (shown up to 9) at $834E, the three Q-token digits ($6B, $6A) at $835B-$835D, the seven score digits from $9D-$A0 ending at $83AE, then five bars from table $8649, left to right: armour $96F0 at $8389, $5B at $838B, $5D, $5F and $59 together at $838D, $5A at $838F, the lasers $5C at $8391.

Tests the car's box (x $96E2 + width $96EE, y $96E4 + height $96EF) against every other object with a width (+C), and for each overlap calls the collision handler for its kind (+F, low five bits) from the tables at $8F33 (low bytes) and $8F53 (high), with ($04) pointing at the object. Returns the number of hits in A ($8E).

Tests each live shot of the 16 at $9A22 (life +8) against the objects. A shot with +1 at 0 (the car's) can hit any object whose kind (+F) is not 0 and has bit 7 clear; a shot with +1 set (an enemy's) is tested only against the car. On a hit it takes the shot's damage (+E) from the object's hit points (+E). If they last, a spark ($2D23); if not, the score ($2C9F) and the kind's hit handler from $8EF3/$8F13. Unless the shot's +7 is set it then ends (life 1). Returns the number of hits ($8E).

The same test for the car's weapon objects (kind 0 with a width, from slot 1) against every object of kinds 1 to 127. A negative damage (+E) pushes the target aside ($2D72); otherwise hit points, spark, score and hit handler as in $2ABF. A weapon without +7 is removed after its first hit.

Adds the object's value (+7, BCD) to the score's hundreds byte $9F, carrying into $9E and $9D, and shows signs worth a tenth of it: $05 one "50", $10 one "100", $25 two "100"s and a "50" fanning out, $50 five "100"s ($2712).
Sound 5 and a small burst (frame $2D, script $9065, colour 2, or 11 when $58 is set) 12 pixels left and 8 up from the point in $17/$18.
An RTS that nothing calls.
Gives the object at ($04) a random x speed from -8 to 7.

Sound 4. Turns the object at ($04) into its explosion: gives back its hardware sprite, clears its width and link id, restarts its animation on script $9027 (or $903C when $58 is set) with handler $30AC, which does nothing.
Hit handler: refills the object's hit points to 50 and counts $77 down; at 0 kills every object of kind $1B ($2D7E) with its score and clears $7C.
Hit handler: sets the car's armour to 0.
Hit handler: counts $77 down (clearing $7C at 0), kills the object and starts the explosion on its linked part (+11/+12) too.
Hit handler: kills the object and removes its linked part.
Run by the homing weapon ($174A) on the object kept in $7A: if it shows frame $31, kills it with its score, clears the target ($76) and removes its two linked parts with their sprites.
Collision kind 1: slows the car (one more y speed, clearing $40 at 0), the object takes frame $58 and loses its width; sound 13.
Collision kind 3: 5 off the armour; the object takes frame $68 and loses its width.
Collision kind 2: sound 14, the car spins (script $8F97, $41 set, delay 1) and keeps moving; the object takes frame $4D.

Collision kind 4: sound 4 and 10 off the armour. When that empties it, the car crashes: controls locked ($40, $42), a crash script by its sideways direction ($90E8 or $90F6), y speed -1 if it was standing. The object takes frame $47.

Collision kind 5. If the car is more than 8 pixels into it, sound 12, 500 points off the score (not below 0, shown by a "-50" sign) and the object's animation jumps to step $1A, taking the car's y speed less 1 on land. Otherwise it steps aside, left or right at random.
Collision kind 6: sound 10, the object loses its width, takes the car's y speed less 1, script $8FFF (or $900A on water), and goes left or right at random.
Collision kind 7: 10 off the armour, the object loses its width and sparks ($2D23).
Collision kind 9: sound 10, the object loses its width, moves with the scroll and goes left or right at random.
Collision kind 13: 10 off the armour and the object explodes ($2D7E).
Collision kind 20: sound 9, removes the object and adds one Q token to the BCD count $6A/$6B.
An RTS: the handler of objects that do nothing, and the collision handler of kinds that do nothing.

Collision with another vehicle (kinds 10, 11, 16, 17, 21-23): sound 3 and sparks ($391D). If either is moving sideways they swap x speeds and the other loses a hit point (exploding with its score when they run out); otherwise both go back to their last y. The car is nudged one pixel away from it.
Part of $30AD for a head-on bump (neither moving sideways): both go back to their last y.

Collision kind 14, the Q-truck. If the car is 176 to 193 lines below it and not spinning ($41), the car is taken in: controls locked ($42), $69 set negative for $1422, frame 1, script $90CD. Otherwise a shunt like $30AD that moves the truck's two parts with it.
Part of $310D for a head-on bump: the truck and its two parts go back to their last y (parts 21 lines below).
Collision kind 12: sound 3, sparks and one off the armour; the object loses a hit point (killed with its part, $2E5D, when they run out), otherwise a shunt that moves its linked part with it.
Part of $31BD for a head-on bump: the object and its part go back to their last y.

Collision kind 24: locks the controls ($42) and restarts the car's animation, its delay reload set from its y speed (at least 1). On water uses script $8FAB. On land with frame 0 and $65 set uses script $907A; with frame 0 and no $65 sparks and script $8FA3. Otherwise, by which side of it the car is on, sets $40 and steers the car left ($3C82) or right ($3CA2).

Collision handler for a pickup: sound 8, removes it, and by its frame (+3) fills a weapon. $38 or $6B: lasers ($5C = 31). $00: $59 = 31. $39: $5D = 31. $6C: $5F = 31. $37 or $6A: $60 on. $3A or $6D: $61 on. $3B or $69: full armour ($96F0 = $FF).
Lasers to 31 ($5C).
Turns $5E on ($FF).
Turns $60 on ($FF).
Turns $61 on ($FF).

Shot handler: kills the object ($2D7E), clears $7C, moves the explosion centre ($75/$76) by +32 and -32, and throws debris ($3357).

Sound 4, then adds 31 debris objects around ($75, $76), each 0 to 63 pixels right and down at random, with random frame offset 0-7 ($2C) and animation script $901F, or $9034 when $58 is set. Stops early when x passes 255.
Steps the random number at $80 (times 5 plus 1), the same sequence as the frame tick, and returns it.
Collision handler: explodes the other object ($2D23) unless $6E is still counting (then sets it to 4), and takes 5 from the armour ($96F0), stopping at 0.

Returns in A the character in the buffer under screen position X,Y ($E242 + 32 per row, from y - 40 and x / 8 - 1). Returns 0 when y is outside $32-$CB.

Sets the scroll speed $82 from the car's height on the screen ($96E4): 6 above $5A, then 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 at $69, $78, $87, $96 and $AB, and 0 below $AB, where the car is held. Speed 6 while $46 counts down. With $4C set ($346E) or during the Q-truck sequence ($7C) the speed is fixed.

Draws the 16 shots of 15 bytes at $9A22 as characters into the screen being built ($7800 or $7C00 by $9B). Copies the 128 bytes at $E1C2 into characters $F0-$FF ($7780), then writes each visible shot's character number ($F0 upwards) into the screen at its cell.
From the last shot back, counts each live shot's life (+8) down and puts back the screen character it covered (+D).

Adds an enemy shot from the template position ($22, $24) towards the car: the x and y distances are halved together until both are below 15, signs restored, and the scroll speed taken from y. Life 20, two rows high ($30). Ends in $10EC.

Reads keyboard row $DC01. The C= key toggles the music ($F4; tune 8 on, 0 off). SPACE pauses: waits for it to be released, pressed and released again. In sections 3 and 4 the joystick goes to $3840 instead.

The car's controls. Up and down ($3C57, $3C6C) change the y speed $96E8, left and right ($3C82, $3CA2) the x speed $96E7; fire runs $39F2. Not while the controls are locked ($42, $41) or $46 runs. Picks the car's frame from the x speed ($869F on land, $86AC on water, $6E or $11 while $40 is set), alternating frames $01/$18 and $92/$99 to animate while it moves.
Controls for sections 3 and 4: the joystick sets x and y speeds in steps up to 4 ($3CC2-$3CE3), which ease back to 0 every fifth pass when it is let go. Frames from $86B9 (scene kind 2) or $86C2.
Counts the timers $6C, $6D, $6E and $3E down to 0, and $3D only while fire is not held ($67).
Takes one from the armour ($96F0) and, every fourth call ($6C), adds a puff (frame $2D, script $9069) below the car, 8 pixels left or right at random.

Reached at the end of the dying animation. Swaps the overlay in, clears the screen ($1944), clears $62-$64. With no lives left shows the message at $8888 and restarts the game ($0C11); otherwise shows the message at $886D and restarts the current section ($43).
Tile kind 3 on land: locks the controls ($42), sound 13, stops the car and gives it frame $71 with animation script $908B, which plays the jump.

Fire pressed. Every fourth pass ($6D) drops a puff behind the car while $5A lasts. Then, unless $3D still counts (reset to 4), plays sound 2 and fires every weapon that has ammunition, in turn: $59 ($3ACE), the lasers $5C ($3B24) and $5B ($3B78). Unless $66 is set it then fires the normal shot straight up ($10EC) and one set of extras: $5D ($3C15, when $3E has run out), or else $5E ($3C21), or else $60 ($3C27), $5F ($3BF5) and $61 ($3C45) together.
Sound 1 and one less $59: adds an object below the car (frame $0E, script $90D7) moving left and down with the car's y speed.
Sound 11 and one less laser ($5C): adds a laser object (frame $36, 8 by 21, script $90CF) at the car moving up 8 faster than the car.
Only when there is a target ($76): one less $5B, sound 1, an object (frame $5D, handler $174A) aimed at ($75, $76), with speeds one eighth of the distance.
One less $5F: three shots with the speeds at $8698 and $869B.
One less $5D and $3E set to 14: eight shots with the speeds at $8688 and $8690.
Four shots, speeds $8688 and $8690 (the first four).
Two shots, speeds $8688 and $8690.
One shot from 16 pixels below, moving down.

One less x speed, to -4.
One more x speed, to 4.
Unlocks the controls ($41, $42, $40 cleared), clears the frame offset and sets the car's animation script to $90CD.
Zeros up to the sprite area, unused.

Sprite frames $00-$1F, 64 bytes each in VIC bank 1. The panel's character set: 64 characters at $8000-$81FF, the part of the panel's own screen ($8000) that is never shown, since only rows 21-24 of that screen are displayed. The panel runs in extended background colour mode, which uses only characters 0-63: digits at 8-17 ($86F0), the bar pieces at $20 and $34-$3A ($8649), letters and the 007 picture.
Bytes after the panel's 64 characters, in the screen's hidden rows: they look like pairs of small digits but no code reads them.

Runs every object once a pass: the 32 slots of 26 bytes from $96E2, the player's car first. A slot whose y (+2) is 0 is free. For each, keeps y as the previous y (+17) and calls the object's handler (+13/+14) with ($0E) pointing at the slot and $8A holding its y, returning to $842C. Then moves it: y by its y speed (+6) and the scroll speed $82, x by its x speed (+5), held to 1-255. An object that leaves the top or bottom is freed with its hardware sprite ($84A2). Then steps its animation ($84C3).
Frees the slot: clears y, the link id (+18) and the width (+C), and gives back its hardware sprite (+15) when it has one.
Stores the animation delay counted down by $84C3.

Gives hardware sprite Y back: clears its entry in the slot list at $A5, clears its expand bits in $94 and $95 (masks $8619) and sets its multicolour bit in $96 ($8611), and asks for the registers to be rewritten ($97).

The animation script interpreter. Counts the delay (+B) down and, when it runs out, reloads it from +1 and reads the next byte of the script at (+8/+9), index +A. A non-zero byte is the next frame (+3). A 0 is followed by a command: a positive number jumps to that index (a loop), $FF removes the object, and anything else is a set of flags each followed by its value: bit 0 x speed (negated when the object is flipped, +19), bit 1 y speed, bit 2 colour, bit 3 width, bit 4 height, bit 5 any field (offset, value), bit 6 a routine to jump to (two bytes), run with the script's place saved.
Script command bit 0: sets the x speed (+5), negated when the object is flipped (+19).
Script command bit 1: sets the y speed (+6).
Script command bit 2: sets the colour (+4).
Script command bit 3: sets the width (+C) used by the collision tests.
Script command bit 4: sets the height (+D).
Script command bit 5: writes a value into any field of the object (two bytes: offset, value).
Script call: flips the object's mirror flag (+19, all bits inverted), so the x speeds of the script's next pass run the other way ($8565). Called at the end of the weaving paths $938C and $93BB.
Zeros to the end of the page.
$8600 keeps X in the busy wait ($1130); $8601/$8602 hold the end-of-frame routine's address, $119F by default ($11B1).
The low byte of the routine the interrupt jumps to at the end of each frame (JMP ($8601) at $12EF), set by $11B1.
The high byte of the end-of-frame routine.
Points added for every row the map scrolls, by speed 0-6: 0, 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36 (the speed squared, in BCD), then the doubled table 0, 2, 8, 18, 32, 50, 72 used while $40 is set ($0D0D).
The eight sprite bits 1, 2, 4 ... 128, for the x high bit and the register masks ($1C88, $84A2).
The same bits inverted, to clear a sprite's bit.
The car's highest x speed right ($8621) and left ($8629) for each y speed, so it cannot steer sharply while slow ($3774).
The car's x speed limits to the left, 0 to -6, indexed by speed.

The shot's pixels to set with $58 ($34C0).
Half-character masks used for shots in sections with $48 set.

X speeds of the eight-shot and four-shot bursts ($3C2B); y speeds at $8690, added to the car's.
Y speeds of the bursts, -6 to 6.
X speeds of the three-way shot ($3BF5), entries 1-3; y speeds at $869B.
Y speeds of the three-way shot.
The car's frame for each sideways speed on land, -6 to 6 ($3774).
The boat's frame for each sideways speed ($3774).
Frames for the free controls of sections 3 and 4 in open water ($3840), by sideways speed -4 to 4.
Frames for the free controls in section 4 ($3840).
Eight link ids, one picked at random to release a waiting object ($27AD).
X positions of the seven pieces of spawn routine 26 ($244C); y positions at $86DA.
Y positions of the formation's pieces.
Offsets into the large ship's picture for drawing fewer rows near the top ($1821).
Colours of the five pickups in the other palette ($231A).
Digit characters: 0-9 of the panel font ($86F0, chars 8-17) and of the play-area font ($86FA, chars $F6-$FF) for the high-score table and the shop.
The panel's three rows of characters ($8704, $8724, $8744) and their colours ($8764, $8784, $87A4), copied in at start-up ($44FA): lives, score, weapon labels and the 007 picture.
The large ship drawn in characters ($1821): 8 rows of 16 character codes.
Offsets of the nine high-score entries in the table at $40E9, 7 bytes apart.
Four bytes nothing reads.
The delay before the panel's switch for each fine-scroll value, so it lands on the same line ($128C).
The value for $D011 at the panel for each fine-scroll value: extended background mode with the matching vertical scroll.
The five messages in lower-case ASCII, each ending in 0: "  get ready" ($8861), "bad show james" ($886D), "  well done" ($887C), "  game over" ($8888) and "congratulations" ($8894).
The byte after the last message.

The sections' spawn lists, three bytes an entry (distance low, distance high, kind) read by $0C17, in one run: section 0 from $88A4 flowing into section 1 at $8A03 (which ends with a stop at $8A75), section 2 from $8A7B (ending in event 3 at $8CCD, which starts it again), section 3 from $8CD3 and section 4 from $8D6F (ending with a stop at $8EA1).

The four start x positions in open water.
Addresses of the 32 spawn routines, by the low five bits of a spawn entry's kind ($0C17).

The high bytes of the hit handlers, by collision kind ($2B5A, $2C56).

The high bytes of the collision handlers, by collision kind ($2A9D).

The sound player, called once a frame by the panel interrupt ($11BB) while a tune plays ($E962). For each of the three voices whose note has ended ($E98C-$E98E) it reads the next commands ($EB6D), with the voice's order list taken from the tune's six bytes at $F43F (two per voice, patched into the readers at $EBB5, $F0F3, $F102 and $F11D). Each voice's settings are kept in a shadow of its seven SID registers ($E970-$E984) and written to the SID ($D400-$D414) unless that voice is resting ($E9C2-$E9C4); voice 3 is left alone for tunes from 40 on (offset $EF). The filter and volume shadows ($E985-$E988) are written every time.

One voice's work for the frame (X = $E965, its SID offset in $E964). While its note lasts runs the effects ($EDEC). Otherwise reads the voice's pattern at ($F7), ($F9) or ($FB) at index $E96C: $FF ends the pattern and takes the next entry of the order list ($EBB1); anything else is a note or a command ($EC2D).

Reads the voice's next order-list byte ($F49F + the voice's index $E966; the address is patched per tune). $FF stops the tune: clears $E962, releases the three gates and returns past the player. A positive byte selects a pattern ($EC14). $E8 sets the volume from the next byte. Other bytes with bit 7 set are order commands: bits 0-4 are a value ($E963) and bits 5-6 choose, through the branch patched at $EC04, transpose ($F0FE, bits 00), repeat count ($F12A, 01), detune ($F0EF, 10) or an instrument map entry ($F10D, 11).
The low byte of the order-list address read at $EBB4, patched per voice by $E9E1.
The high byte of the order-list address in the instruction at $EBB4, patched with each voice's pointer from the tune table by $E9E1 (low byte at $EBB5).
The offset of the BEQ at $EC03, patched with 0, 4, 8 or 12 by $EBB1 to choose one of the four order commands that follow.
Transpose: the first of four JMPs padded to four bytes with a NOP, so the branch offsets 0, 4, 8 and 12 at $EC04 land on each.
The four jumps chosen by the patched branch at $EC03: transpose ($F0FE), repeat ($F12A), detune ($F0EF) and instrument map ($F10D).
Points the voice's pattern pointer ($F7 + 2 per voice) at pattern Y from the tables at $F407 (low bytes) and $F423 (high), and starts it at index 0.

A pattern byte. Below $80 a note ($ED2D). $A0: a rest of the next byte's length, with the gate released. $A1 and $A2: turn the voice's filter routing on or off ($E987, bits $F14A). $90-$9F: picks the arpeggio table ($E9B0, 8 bytes each). $BF: ends a slide. $C0 and up: a slide, with its direction in bit 5 and delay, size (two bytes) and length from the next bytes. $80-$8F: an instrument ($ECC4).

Sets the voice's instrument from the low four bits, through the instrument map at $F18B (copied from $F1A3 at each tune's start), to an entry of the instruments at $F582, copying its bytes into the voice's shadow registers and effect settings.
The operand of the ADD at $ECC7: the player stores 0, 8 or 16 here for voices 1, 2 and 3 ($E9E1), so each voice reads its own eight entries of the instrument map at $F18B.

Starts a note: adds the voice's transpose ($E969) and 20, looks up the frequency ($F1BB low, $F21B high) plus the detune ($E99B), opens the gate, takes the note's length from the next pattern byte, and resets the vibrato ($F156), wave ($F182/$F17E) and arpeggio ($F5C2) steps.

Runs while a note lasts. At the instrument's release point ($E992) closes the gate. Counts the rest and the note down; on later frames runs the slide (adding or taking the step at $E9B6/$E9B9 from the frequency), the pulse-width sweep ($F14E), the vibrato ($F156, eight steps either way), the waveform steps ($F182/$F17E) and the arpeggio ($F5C2, adding semitones to the note).

Starts tune A (each tune is six bytes at $F43F). With the sound switched off ($F4 = 0) only tune 0 is started, and only when nothing is playing. Restarts the three voices (gates pulsed off), points every voice at the empty pattern at $F14D, clears the player's state ($E989-$E9DF), copies the instrument map from $F1A3, and sets full volume ($E988 = 15) and the playing flag ($E962). The game calls it for every sound: 0 silence, 2 the shot, 4 an explosion, 5 a spark, 8 a pickup, 9 a Q token, 13 the ramp and others.
